analysis:
The PR adds an `env.CI_ACTIONS_CACHE != 'off'` guard to every actions/cache restore and save step in the two composite actions. In provider-ci-build/action.yml these are the SwiftPM repos, lane Swift build and Metal cache steps at head lines 64, 91, 146, 154, 160 and 181. In provider-release-build/action.yml they are the Swift build cache, metallib, MiMo audio codec and Swift save steps at head lines 120, 165, 185, 263, 275 and 392. The ci-master.yml patch excerpt shows a new first step that sets CI_ACTIONS_CACHE=off through GITHUB_ENV. It sets it only when the runner is a darkbloom-* Sandbox with no DARKBLOOM_CACHE_URL. That keeps such runners from reaching GitHub's own Actions cache. Rewording of the .git cache step comments, to 'discard unless it can run nothing and git fsck accepts it', is also visible in the excerpt.

Security effect: this is a narrowing change. It reduces the cache-poisoning and cross-trust-boundary reuse surface for build outputs that feed signed provider artifacts (T-034, T-054, A-011, A-017). No new input, secret or permission is introduced. I found no regression in the supplied source. The Save steps are gated on the same flag, so a skipped restore cannot yield a save under an unvalidated key. Downstream steps still revalidate source timestamps, delete cached mlx.metallib, and rebuild or validate the metallib via fetch-metallib.sh (head lines 130-137 and 171-183 of the release action). With the cache off, empty `cache-hit` and `cache-matched-key` outputs fall through to a cold-build path, which affects availability and time, not trust.

Limits: the ci-master.yml unit is metadata only, and its patch excerpt is truncated. I did not see the other changed ranges (roughly head lines 77-290), including the replaced 'Discard a damaged cached .git' step and the `.git` cache validation. A later pass should check that the new .git hook and fsck validation is sound. It should also check that the env-flag step runs before every cache step in each job of that workflow, and that no workflow-level `env:` overrides it. The shell step name and `if` syntax in composite actions look correct.
